samples.summary: No test exercises the summary's population split under a trim, and the split is computed from partial data
samples.evidence: `renderDeferredSummary` computes `demoted = rows.filter(r => r.lane === 'backlog').length` from the records it is GIVEN (deferred-findings.mjs:296), but prints `${total - demoted} non-blocking, ${demoted} demoted` against the FULL `total` (line 300). `buildDeferredCheck` passes only `records.slice(0, emitted)` (line 362), so once the trim fires the two numbers come from different populations: 60 findings of which 30 demoted, trimmed to 10 emitted with 5 demoted, renders "55 non-blocking, 5 demoted". The two tests that could catch this each avoid the combination: "the summary splits the two populations rather than pooling them" (test line 280) builds an UNTRIMMED check with 3 findings, and "the summary states the omission when the record is partial" (test line 290) trims but only asserts /PARTIAL/ and /N were dropped/ — never the split line, and its fixture is 60 identical native minors (demoted === 0 either way), so the arithmetic cannot be wrong in it. The trimmed `buildDeferredCheck` test (line 272) asserts only `/not recorded/` in the title. The module's headline claim is tally honesty ("a reader who never opens `text` still has to be told the list is partial", line 269-270); the honesty of the split under trim is the one part of that claim with no assertion behind it.
searchedFor: grep maxChars / MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS in the test file

samples.summary: "the default budget is ... 60k" only re-asserts a constant against its own literal; nothing proves the default is used
samples.evidence: The test body is `assert.equal(MAX_TEXT_CHARS, 60000)` (test line 196-198). It cannot fail for any behavioural reason — it restates the literal at deferred-findings.mjs:93. No test calls `buildDeferredText`/`buildDeferredCheck` with a payload large enough to overflow the DEFAULT budget: every trim test passes `maxChars` explicitly (test lines 169, 182, 188, 222, 274), and the only default-budget call (test line 156) has a single tiny record. So a regression changing the default to e.g. 5000 while leaving the exported constant at 60000 would pass the whole suite, which is precisely what this test is titled to prevent.

samples.summary: `MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS` clipping of the human body is never exercised by any test
samples.evidence: `renderDeferredSummary` ends with `clip(out.join("\n"), MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS)` (deferred-findings.mjs:321), and the summary grows with the number of distinct `lens`/`severity` tally rows, which under a 60k `text` budget can reach thousands of rows — a reachable path. `MAX_SUMMARY_CHARS` appears nowhere in deferred-findings.test.mjs (it is not even imported, unlike MAX_TEXT_CHARS), and no test asserts a summary length bound, so removing the clip or mis-sizing it is invisible to the suite.
searchedFor: read the full test file import list

samples.summary: The CLI's usage/exit-2 path for missing `--lenses` or `--out-json` has no test
samples.evidence: `main` exits 2 with a usage line when either required flag is absent (deferred-findings.mjs:402-405). The two end-to-end tests cover the happy path (test line 324) and the unreadable-manifest exit 1 (test line 353) only; there is no invocation of the CLI without `--lenses` or without `--out-json`, so a regression that silently defaulted `out-json` (writing a file somewhere unintended) or exited 0 would not be caught.
searchedFor: read both END TO END tests

samples.summary: `readLensFindings`' injected `read`/`exists` seam is never used by any test
samples.evidence: `readLensFindings(reviewDir, manifest, { read = readFileSync, exists = existsSync })` (deferred-findings.mjs:378) exposes an injection point; the only test of it (test line 308) writes real files in a tmpdir and passes no third argument, so the parameterised path is unexercised — a wiring mistake there (e.g. `read` ignored) would be silent. Either drop the seam or cover it.

samples.summary: The `file` fallback to `finding.file` in `deferredRecord` is untested (and may be unreachable)
samples.evidence: `const file = str(loc?.file).trim() || str(finding.file).trim() || undefined;` (deferred-findings.mjs:167). `findingLocation` (novelty.mjs:157-188) already returns `{file, line:null}` whenever `finding.file` is a non-empty string, so the second operand can only matter for shapes no test constructs; no test in deferred-findings.test.mjs passes a finding where `loc.file` is empty but `finding.file` is set. Either the branch is dead or it guards a case nothing proves.
searchedFor: grep deferredRecord assertions on .file in the test file

verdict.reason: The factual absence is real — I confirmed no test anywhere (only test file for this module; workflow at agent-review-panel.yml:1088-1125 invokes it untested; no .trusted copy) exercises renderDeferredSummary with a trim AND mixed populations, so the arithmetic mismatch between `demoted` (from records.slice(0, emitted), deferred-findings.mjs:296/362) and `total` (line 300) has no assertion behind it. But it is not blocking under the test-adequacy rubric. Both constituent behaviors have meaningful, non-vacuous tests: the population split is asserted at deferred-findings.test.mjs:280-288 (/2 non-blocking, 1 demoted/ fails if the split is pooled or miscounted), and partial-record honesty is asserted at 290-296 plus 165-178 and 186-194 (fail if the trim stops reporting total/omitted). What is missing is the cross-product of two separately-covered behaviors, which the rubric defines as minor ("coverage could be broader but the core behavior is tested"), and the rubric forbids flagging "add more tests" as a blocker unless a behavior has no meaningful test at all. Whether the mixed-population arithmetic is itself wrong is a correctness-lens question about non-test code, explicitly out of this lane. No vacuous assertion and no over-mocking is present in the cited tests.
